scope: Bounded hunch generation over authenticated completed GEO CourtListener/RECAP case reports, verified findings, the completed coverage audit, and existing hypotheses; no new court search
filters: already captured in a finding, prior synthesis, or existing hypothesis
three or more independent contexts rather than multiple proceedings in one dispute family
not an obvious consequence of federal-contractor litigation
genuinely surprising to an investigator familiar with the portfolio
distinguishes coordination from ordinary aligned incentives or legal advocacy
produces a nonduplicative Layer-1 research plan
preserves holding, allegation, contract-text, party-position, and inference boundaries

candidates.candidate: Issue-specific allocation of GEO and ICE control recurs across detainee labor and facility inspection
candidates.reason: The mechanism is already explicit in findings 12557, 12737, 12741-12744, 12762, and 12780 and in the completed detainee-labor and inspection case reports. Registering it would relabel existing work rather than commission a new test.

candidates.candidate: GEO repeatedly uses Yearsley, preemption, intergovernmental immunity, and federal-control arguments across disputes
candidates.reason: Repeated use of available federal-contractor doctrines is expected advocacy. Holdings vary, and Delaney Hall is only an unadjudicated party position. No common agency instruction or counsel-direction record was recovered.

candidates.candidate: Federal litigation positions are organizationally compartmentalized across ICE, DOJ, and procurement actors
contexts: Delaney Hall DOJ Statement of Interest
candidates.reason: The observed variation is real but ordinary for issue-specific government litigation. ICE/OPLA awareness and planned engagement followed by adverse contracting-officer decisions further separates access from favorable coordination. No agency memoranda, common referral chain, or contradictory instruction establishes an internal compartmentalization mechanism.

candidates.candidate: GEO shifts detainee-labor defense costs to ICE through reimbursement, indemnity, or equitable adjustment
candidates.recurrence_filter: pass only as one coordinated three-vehicle batch
candidates.reason: Authenticated records show GEO requested reimbursement and DOJ defense and ICE denied all three REAs in full; the Northwest contract separately assigned litigation cost to GEO. Finding 13016 records that June 2018 allocation. The evidence does not show a recurring successful cost shift, permanent bar, later payment, or portfolio-wide policy, so no new hypothesis or lead is warranted. Lead 63588 is completed.

candidates.candidate: GEO follows a uniform inspection-access resistance policy across federal detention facilities
candidates.reason: NWIPC produced adjudicated access orders and area carveouts; Delaney Hall inspection occurred and the emergency motion was withdrawn; a Washington L&I comparison ended in stipulated access. The record shows contested boundaries, not one proven policy.

candidates.candidate: Subsidiary and legacy-entity structure compartmentalizes litigation liability away from GEO parent operations
candidates.reason: Roycroft is a pre-acquisition attribution problem and Burciaga lacks the payer and contract. Neither establishes deliberate risk routing, and there are fewer than three independent, properly attributed contexts.

candidates.candidate: Adverse GEO litigation is structurally compartmentalized from ICE procurement and contract consequences
candidates.reason: This substantially duplicates hypotheses 335/336 and completed runs 94/95. Finding 12619 already records the non-discriminating action-timing test, while the required responsibility, CPARS, legal-review, option, invoice, and deduction records are already commissioned.

reconsideration_triggers: Authenticated ICE/GEO litigation-direction or common-counsel instructions across three independent facility contexts
Complete contracts showing express ICE direction of the challenged practice rather than reimbursement or baseline standards
Later authenticated reimbursement, compensating modification, appeal, voucher, or DOJ representation that reverses or materially qualifies the June 2018 denials
A common access-control clause and internal implementation policy producing the same adjudicated result at three facilities
Responsibility, CPARS, source-selection, option, or suspension/debarment records showing non-routine litigation treatment after matched controls
interpretation: The portfolio supports a bounded systemic description—control is allocated by actual direction, practice, space, and contract-administration decision. Newly authenticated records show a 2018 three-vehicle request-and-denial mechanism, not reimbursement or coordinated insulation. The remaining hunch candidates either duplicate existing records or fail recurrence, intent, or attribution gates.
